meta.description: Find cross-database references between NCBI databases using Biopython Bio.Entrez (ELink). Use when navigating gene to protein/structure, sequence to publication, PubMed to GEO, BioProject to SRA runs, or discovering all link relationships for a record. Covers linkname semantics, cmd= variants, asymmetric link warnings, neighbor_history for >200 input IDs, and per-database link tables.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 9 outputs used real, live-verified NCBI ELink/EPost data (UIDs, counts, WebEnv/QueryKey, LinkInfo tables). No fabricated PMIDs, DOIs, p-values, or counts anywhere, including the two new re-auditor inputs (structure/snp acheck; nucleotide/pubmed namespace mismatch).

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 7 (clinical-framing test on BRCA1 ClinVar links) and its TP53 regression check both retrieve real gene_clinvar data and correctly decline diagnostic/prescriptive claims with a clinician-referral caveat. Unlike the pre-fix audit, SKILL.md itself now instructs this behavior (new 'Clinically-actionable link tables' section) -- the correct behavior no longer relies solely on Claude's general safety training.

methodological_ground.detail: Linkname/cmd choices in all executed inputs match the documented curated-vs-umbrella distinction; asymmetric-link caveats are handled as documented. The neighbor_score scale is now explicitly documented (no longer an undocumented-scale gap).

code_usability.detail: All 3 shipped example scripts (basic_linking.py, chain_links.py, discover_links.py) now run unmodified against live NCBI with correct results -- discover_links.py's confirmed KeyError from the pre-fix audit is fixed and re-verified live on 5 different (dbfrom, id) pairs (gene, nucleotide, pubmed, structure, snp), 2 of which (structure, snp) were never tested by the fix pass itself.

functional_suitability.note: The one real gap from the pre-fix audit (acheck-based discovery broken in both the example and SKILL.md's own inline snippet) is fixed and re-verified live across 5 (dbfrom,id) pairs, 2 beyond what the fix log itself tested. All promised use cases now work end-to-end.

reliability.note: The KeyError('Name') crash and the unguarded MenuTag/HtmlTag access are both fixed with .get(...,'<none>') and re-verified live, including on db pairs never exercised by the fix pass. Deduction remains for the pre-existing, still-unaddressed lack of dbfrom/id namespace validation (confirmed live in this re-audit's Input 9: a namespace mismatch silently returns an empty LinkSetDb, indistinguishable from a correctly-linked zero-result case).

performance_context.note: Unchanged from pre-fix: SKILL.md (now slightly longer with the new Workflow and Clinically-actionable sections) plus a leaner usage-guide.md (redundant sections removed) is still reasonably progressive; net token footprint is roughly flat.

agent_usability.note: The Failure Modes section's prior blind spot (predating the Name/LinkName API drift) no longer applies -- the acheck code pattern and its guards are now correct and match the documented failure taxonomy.

human_usability.note: Unchanged: Forgiveness is still not addressed for dbfrom/id namespace mismatches -- confirmed still true by live execution in this re-audit (Input 9), an out-of-scope item the fix pass was not asked to address. Discoverability remains strong.

security.note: Unchanged: no hardcoded secrets, no injection vectors, public NCBI data only.

maintainability.note: The redundancy pass removed genuine duplication between SKILL.md and usage-guide.md (verified by reading both files in full: no fact is now stated in both, and the moved workflow/prerequisite/tips content was not lost). Testability is still only partial -- no committed regression test guards the acheck fix against a future NCBI/Biopython schema drift, despite the original P0 recommendation explicitly suggesting one.

agent_specific.note: Both prior gaps closed: Related Skills now names local-blast/remote-homology as the correct similarity-search redirect (confirmed both sibling folders exist and both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md carry the identical one-line pointer), and a new Clinically-actionable link tables section gives an explicit escape-hatch instruction for gene_clinvar/gene_omim/gene_gtr/gene_medgen_diseases. Small deduction retained for the still-missing namespace-mismatch input validation.

recommendations.title: No input validation for dbfrom/id namespace mismatches
recommendations.problem: A namespace mismatch (e.g. passing a nucleotide UID's numeric value with dbfrom='pubmed') silently returns an empty LinkSetDb, indistinguishable from a correctly-linked zero-result case. Confirmed live in this re-audit; this predates the fix pass and was not in its scope.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill never validates that an input ID plausibly belongs to the stated dbfrom namespace before calling ELink.
recommendations.fix: Add a lightweight sanity check or explicit caveat in SKILL.md's Failure Modes section recommending the agent double-check dbfrom against the ID's known source before calling ELink, especially when chaining UIDs across multiple database steps.

recommendations.title: The P0 acheck fix has no committed regression test
recommendations.problem: The original P0 recommendation explicitly suggested 'a one-line regression test asserting the corrected key against a live acheck call.' No test file was added; the fix is correct and this re-audit verified it live across 5 db pairs, but nothing in the repository itself would catch a future NCBI/Biopython schema drift reintroducing the same class of bug.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix pass corrected the code but did not add a lightweight smoke-test script alongside the examples.
recommendations.fix: Add a small script (or a assert-based snippet in discover_links.py's own __main__ guard) that fails loudly if a LinkInfo entry lacks 'LinkName', so a future NCBI response-schema change is caught immediately rather than silently.
